a1-n-raum: You carry a big wardrobe into a flat. The agent says the empty area inside the walls is large enough for it and for a bed too.
At work you ask whether the office has enough free space for two more desks.
You are in the kitchen, the bedroom and the bathroom of a new flat. Each one is a separate enclosed area with its own door. Which word fits?
a1-v-umziehen: Your rent went up, so next month you will pack all your boxes and start living in a different flat.
You come home from work in a suit and put on jeans and a T-shirt instead.
Your company needs you in another city, so your whole family has to go and live there.
a1-n-zentimeter: You use a ruler to measure a pencil. Each numbered mark on the ruler is one hundredth of a metre.
The tailor says your waist is 82 of these, a unit equal to ten millimetres.
A nurse measures how tall you are and says: one metre and seventy-two of what? Which unit, written 'cm', is meant?
a1-adj-frei: You ask a waiter if you can sit at a table and he says nobody has booked it, so you can use it.
At the toilet door the lock shows green: nobody is inside.
It is Sunday and you have no work and no plans. Your schedule is empty all day.
a1-n-blick: From the hotel balcony you can see the mountains and the lake. What a beautiful ... from this window!
You quickly look at your phone for one second and then put it away again.
Your cat stares at you with a long, serious gaze while you eat your fish.
a1-adv-hinten: The bus is full, so the driver tells you to walk to the end of the bus, behind everyone else.
In the cinema you sit in the very last row, far from the screen.
You look for the toilets in the restaurant and the waiter says they are at the rear of the room.
a1-n-thema: The teacher asks what you want to talk about in your presentation. You say it is about healthy food.
Your friends keep talking about football, but you want to change what the conversation is about.
You write an essay and the first line on the page says what it is about. Which word means 'topic'?
a1-v-sich-fragen: You see your neighbour's lights on at midnight and think quietly to yourself: why is he still awake?
You have not heard from your friend for weeks and you ask yourself what has happened. You do not ask anyone out loud.
After the exam you think silently: did I pass? Which verb describes this kind of silent questioning of yourself?
a1-n-tisch: At home your family eats dinner around a piece of furniture with four legs and a flat top.
In the classroom you put your books and pens on the flat wooden surface in front of your chair.
In a restaurant the waiter says: 'I have reserved a place for four people. It is by the window.' What piece of furniture will you sit at?
a1-pr-sich: Your little brother looks into the mirror and washes his own face. What word shows he does the action to himself?
Anna and Tom are in a hurry. Each of them quickly gets dressed, with no help from the other. Which small word goes with 'he' or 'she' for this?
A doctor says people should look after their own health. Which word shows the person does it for their own self, for he, she, it and they?
a1-n-sehenswuerdigkeit: On your trip to Berlin you visit the old castle and the famous tower that every tourist wants to see.
At the tourist office you ask for a map with all the famous places worth visiting in town.
A friend asks what there is to do in Paris. You say the Eiffel Tower is the main one that visitors come to see.
a1-n-fahrkarte: At the station you buy a small piece of paper from the machine so you may ride the train to Munich.
The conductor walks through the carriage and asks every passenger to show what proves they paid for the journey.
You lose the paper you need for the bus to work and have to buy a new one. Which word means a travel ticket?
a1-v-sollen: The doctor says you must take the medicine twice a day. It is what you are told to do.
Your mother says you ought to call your grandmother more often. What word fits 'I ... call her'?
The sign says the visitors are expected to leave their shoes at the door. Which verb expresses this duty or advice?
a1-adj-weiss: You buy a new shirt for a wedding, the colour of fresh snow and milk.
The doctor wears a coat the colour of fresh printer paper and the clouds on a sunny day.
You mix lots of light into your paint until it becomes the lightest possible colour, like a sheet of paper. Which colour word?
a1-n-fruehling: In March the snow melts, the flowers start to open and the birds come back. It is the season after winter.
You say your favourite time of year is when it gets warmer and the trees get new green leaves, just before summer.
A friend asks which season comes between winter and summer. Which word means 'spring'?
a1-n-oel: You heat a pan and pour a little golden liquid into it before you fry the eggs.
The car makes a loud noise. The mechanic says the engine needs a new liquid to lubricate its parts.
At the salad bar you take the green bottle made from olives and sprinkle some on your food.
a1-v-drucken: You send your essay to the machine in the office so you can hold it on paper.
At the station you need a paper copy of your online booking, so you ask the clerk to put it on paper for you.
Your colleague needs the contract with ink on paper for the meeting in five minutes. Which verb describes making a paper copy from the computer?
a1-n-moment: You are on the phone and say to your friend: wait a very short time, I will be right back.
At a party someone asks you to stand still while she takes a picture at exactly the right instant.
A waiter says he will be with you in just a little while. Which word means a very short period of time?
a1-adv-weiter: You are walking in the mountains and your friend says: let's not stop here, let's keep going onwards.
The teacher stops the story at a good place. The children shout: tell us more, go on!
A sign shows that the train goes beyond this station to the next city. Which word means 'onwards' or 'further'?
a1-n-disco: On Saturday night you dance with friends to loud music and flashing lights.
Your sister is eighteen now, so she can go to the place where young people dance until 3 a.m.
A friend says: let's go out tonight, there is a good DJ at the place with the dance floor. What place?
a1-n-maedchen: In the playground a young female child with long hair is riding a swing.
A mother introduces her daughter, aged seven: this is my little ... Which word means a young female?
At the school party a boy and a young female pupil of ten years old are dancing together.
a1-adj-teuer: You see a coat in a shop window that costs 800 euros. You say you can't pay so much for it.
You have lunch near the tourist centre and the bill is very high for just a soup and a salad.
The price of a flat in the city centre is far more than most people can afford. Which adjective describes the cost?
a1-v-regnen: You look out of the window and see grey clouds and water falling from the sky, so you take an umbrella.
The football match is cancelled because water is pouring down from the sky all afternoon.
A weather report says that tomorrow there will be drops falling from the clouds. Which verb describes this weather?
a1-n-bus: Every morning you stand at the stop and wait for a big yellow vehicle that takes people through the city.
Your school group is going on a trip. The driver opens the door of a large coach with forty seats.
At night the underground stops running, so you take the road vehicle that stops at every street corner.
a1-n-teil: You break a chocolate bar and give your friend one piece. Which word means one piece of a whole?
The mechanic says the car needs a new piece for the engine, but it is out of stock.
The teacher says the first section of the book is easy but the second section is harder.
a1-n-ticket: You buy a pass online to see your favourite band play live on Friday night.
At the airport you show the boarding document on your phone so you can get on the plane.
You queue at the cinema box office and ask for two paper passes to the evening film.
a1-v-reparieren: Your bicycle has a flat tyre, so you get the tools out and make it work again.
The washing machine stopped working, so a technician comes to your flat to make it work again.
Your phone screen is cracked and you take it to a shop. What do they do to the phone?
a1-n-farbe: You are in a paint shop and look at lots of little cards: red, blue, yellow and green. What is each one?
The teacher asks the children which shade they like best for their drawing: red, green or blue.
You want to repaint the kitchen walls, so you buy two big tins of liquid for the wall at the hardware store.
a1-pr-all: The teacher says: please open your books, every single one of you.
The waiter brings the bill and says that everything was perfect, the whole meal.
You enter a room and say hello to every single person in it. Which word means 'everyone' or 'everything'?
a1-adv-wie: You meet a friend and ask about the way she is feeling and doing today.
You want to know the way to do something, like how to cook rice. Which question word do you start with?
You say that your sister is tall in the same way that your mother is tall. Which small word shows the comparison?
a1-n-hund: Every morning your neighbour walks his pet that barks and wags its tail around the park.
At the animal shelter a child asks to take home the friendly furry pet that barks, not the one that meows.
A sign at the shop door says that no pets that bark are allowed inside. What animal is it?
a1-adj-fremd: You arrive in a country where you don't know the language, the food or anyone. Everything feels very new and unknown.
A person you have never seen before knocks at your door. For you this person is a complete stranger.
A letter comes from someone you do not know, and the handwriting is unfamiliar. Which adjective describes something that is not familiar?
a1-v-holen: You are in the kitchen and your mother asks you to go to the cellar and bring a bottle of water.
The teacher asks you to go to the office and come back with the chalk.
Your child is playing outside. You go to the garden to bring him in for dinner.
a1-n-absender: On the back of the envelope there is a name and an address of the person who posted the letter.
You receive a parcel and wonder who sent it. You look at the label at the top left for the name of the person who posted it.
You fill in the post office form. One box asks for your name as the person who is posting the package, the other for the person who gets it.
a1-n-kollegin: At lunch you sit with a woman who works in the same office as you, and she tells you about her weekend.
You introduce Maria, who works next to you at the company, to your friend. Which word describes her?
Your female workmate is ill, so you offer to take over her tasks for the day.
a1-n-kiosk: Before work you buy a newspaper, a bar of chocolate and a bus ticket at the small stand on the street corner.
You are at the station and quickly need a bottle of water and some sweets from the small booth.
A friend asks where you buy magazines and lottery tickets. You point to a tiny shop with a window on the street.
a1-v-besichtigen: On holiday in Rome you walk inside the old cathedral and look at everything with a guide.
The estate agent invites you to look at the flat you may want to rent. You go there to see it.
A school class goes to a factory to look around and see how cars are built.
a1-n-winter: It is December, there is snow on the ground and you wear a thick coat, gloves and a hat.
The three months with the shortest days: December, January and February.
In your country the coldest time of the year is coming. You can ski and the lakes freeze. Which season?
a1-adj-gelb: You peel a ripe banana and see its colour.
In the school bus, painted in a bright sunny colour, children go home.
A child draws the sun and chooses the crayon in the colour of a lemon.
a1-n-partner: Your wife, husband or the person you live with is the one you love and plan your life with.
In a business meeting you say that the other company is someone you work together with on the project.
For the dance class, the teacher says to choose the person who will dance with you. Which word means the person who is paired with you?
a1-n-caf: On Saturday morning you meet a friend in a small place to drink a cappuccino and eat a piece of cake.
You sit at a table outside, read a book and order a coffee from a waiter. Where are you?
Tourists in Vienna are tired and look for a cosy place that serves coffee and pastries.
a1-adv-einmal: You have been to Berlin one time, long ago, and it was beautiful. How many times?
The teacher says: do this exercise one time, then we will check. Which word means 'one time'?
Your grandmother says that in some future day we should all visit the sea together. Which adverb means 'some day'?
a1-v-entschuldigen: You step on a stranger's foot on the bus and say sorry, then you say that you regret what you did.
Your friend is late for the party. When he arrives he says sorry, asking you to forgive him.
You are late for a meeting because of traffic. You ask your boss to forgive you by saying that you are sorry.
a1-n-kartoffel: For dinner your grandmother peels and boils round brown vegetables that grow underground, to eat with fish.
At the fast food restaurant you order the long golden fries; they are made from this vegetable.
You dig in the garden and find round vegetables growing under the soil, used for mashed dishes. Which vegetable?
a1-n-durchsage: At the station a voice from the loudspeaker says that the train to Hamburg is ten minutes late.
In the supermarket a voice over the speakers tells customers that the shop will close in fifteen minutes.
At the airport a speaker tells passengers to go to gate 12. Which word means this spoken notice over a loudspeaker?
a1-n-ort: You tell the taxi driver the spot where you want to be dropped off, the exact location.
You ask where the meeting will be held, and your boss names a small town near Munich.
On the form you write the name of the town where you were born, in the box for the birth place.
a1-v-sterben: The old oak in the garden stopped growing and its leaves turned brown. The tree is slowly ceasing to live.
Your grandfather was very old and ill. One night he passed away peacefully.
The film's hero is shot at the end and his life ends. What verb describes this?
a1-adj-kaputt: You drop your phone and the screen cracks into pieces. Now it does not work any more.
Your coffee machine will not switch on and nothing happens. It is out of order.
The chair leg snaps off when your uncle sits on it. What adjective describes the chair?
a1-n-obst: At the market you buy apples, oranges and bananas and put them in a bowl on the table.
The doctor tells you to eat more sweet things that grow on trees, and fewer cakes.
A shop has a section for apples, pears and grapes, next to the vegetable section. What is that section called?
a1-pr-kein: You open your wallet and see that you do not have even one euro in it. Which word means 'not a single'?
At the shop the clerk says that there are no more tickets for tonight. Which word replaces 'a' in 'not a ticket'?
A friend asks if you have a car. You answer that you have not got one at all. Which word means 'not a'?
a1-n-freitag: The week is almost over. After this working day the weekend starts, and you go out with friends in the evening.
The day between Thursday and Saturday is when many people finish work early.
Your boss says the project must be finished by the last working day of the week. Which day?
a1-v-kriegen: For your birthday you are happy to be given a new bike by your parents.
At the post office you are handed a parcel that you were waiting for. You obtain the package.
You run after the bus and manage to reach it just before the doors close; you catch it.
a1-n-butter: For breakfast you spread something yellow and creamy, made from milk, on your bread.
The recipe says to melt a hundred grams of the yellow dairy fat in the pan before adding the eggs.
At the supermarket you ask where to find the dairy product that goes on bread, next to the cheese.
a1-adv-minus: The weather report says that tomorrow the temperature will be below zero, at three degrees below zero. Which word do you say before 'three'?
In a maths lesson the teacher says: ten take away four is six. Which word do you say for the subtraction sign?
Your bank account shows that you owe money. The number has a sign in front of it. Which word means 'negative'?
a1-n-lebensmittel: On Saturday you go to the supermarket and fill your trolley with bread, milk, vegetables and meat.
At the checkout, the cashier says that everything in your basket is for eating and drinking, so the tax is lower.
A charity collects tins, rice and pasta for people in need. What do they collect?
a1-n-feier: You invite all your friends to your flat to enjoy music, food and cake because it is your birthday.
At work the team has a small event in the kitchen with sparkling wine after a big success.
The family gets together on New Year's Eve with fireworks and drinks. Which word describes this kind of party or event?
a1-v-danken: A stranger helps you carry your heavy bags upstairs, and you tell him you are very grateful.
After the nice dinner, your friend gives you a gift. You smile and say how grateful you are, giving her your thanks.
The teacher helped you with the exam. You want to show gratitude. Which verb means to express thanks?
a1-adj-lieb: Your little niece gives you a hug and a drawing. She is such a sweet, gentle girl.
You begin a letter to a person you like very much: 'Hello, my ... Anna'. Which word fits before her name?
A neighbour brings you soup when you are ill. You tell her she is very kind and nice.
a1-n-leute: The bus is full, and many men, women and children are standing there. You say that a lot of persons are inside.
At the concert there are thousands of persons in the crowd, all singing.
A friend says that some persons in town are unfriendly. Which word means many persons in general?
a1-n-euro: You go to a German shop and give the cashier a coin. The currency is used in Germany, France and Italy.
A coffee costs three of them. What currency do you pay with in Berlin?
You travel from Poland to Germany and exchange your money into the currency used there, which has the sign €.
a1-n-fruehstueck: In the morning you eat bread with jam and drink coffee before you leave for work.
At the hotel you go to the dining room at eight o'clock where there are rolls, cheese and eggs. What meal is that?
Which meal comes first in the day, before lunch and dinner?
a1-v-schicken: You write an email to your teacher and press the button so it goes to her inbox.
You put a birthday card in an envelope and post it to your grandmother in another country.
Your boss asks you to forward the documents to the client by courier. Which verb means to make something go to another person?
a1-n-kleidung: You open your wardrobe and see trousers, shirts, dresses and jackets. What do you wear on your body every day?
At the second-hand shop you donate the things you no longer wear, such as shirts and skirts.
At the airport you pack T-shirts and trousers into your suitcase. What are you packing?
a1-n-gewicht: At the doctor you step onto the scale and the nurse writes how heavy you are: seventy kilos.
At the post office the clerk puts your parcel on the scale to check how heavy it is, to know the cost.
The plane only allows bags that are twenty kilos at most. What does this limit refer to?
a1-adv-vor: The teacher says to the student at the back: please come to the front of the class, move up.
In a queue the person behind you says that you can go ahead, to the front of the line.
The bus driver says: move up in the bus, there is space in the front. Which small word means 'forwards'?
a1-adj-weit: Your village is 200 kilometres away from the city, a long distance from here. Which adjective describes this?
You buy trousers that fit loosely and are not tight at all. They are very roomy.
The river is very broad, so it takes a long time to swim across it.
a1-v-glauben: A friend tells you that it will rain tomorrow. You say that you think so, too, or you accept it as true.
A child says the story is true and he trusts what his father said. He accepts it.
You are not sure if the shop is open. You say that you suppose it is, because it is a weekday.
a1-n-adresse: The postman needs to know the street, house number and city so he can deliver the letter to your home.
You fill in a form and write your street name, number and postcode in the box. What is that information called?
The taxi driver asks where to take you. You give him the name of the street and number of your house.
a1-pr-der: You point at a man and say: that is the man who lives next door. Which small word means 'who'?
The teacher puts three small words in front of nouns, masculine, feminine and neuter, as the definite articles. Which words are they?
You say about a car: 'the car which I bought is red'. Which word means 'which'?
a1-n-kuli: You borrow a small writing instrument with ink inside and a click button from the shop to sign the form.
The teacher says you can use pencil or a blue one with a ball tip for your test.
A colleague lends you the small blue writing tool in his pocket to write the phone number. What is it? A short, informal word.
a1-n-bier: At a Bavarian garden you order a cold glass of golden drink with white foam, made from hops and barley.
On Saturday evening your friends watch football and drink bottles of a drink with 5% alcohol, made from malt.
In Germany people say it is the most famous drink at Oktoberfest, drunk from a big glass mug.
a1-v-buchstabieren: On the phone the clerk can't understand your surname, so you say each letter one by one.
At the hotel reception you say your name letter by letter, M-U-E-L-L-E-R, so the clerk can write it down.
The teacher asks you to say the word out loud, one letter at a time. What is that action?
a1-n-mutter: On Mother's Day you give flowers to the woman who gave birth to you.
A child calls out for the woman who cooks his dinner and puts him to bed. Who is she?
You introduce the woman next to you to your friends: she is my female parent.
a1-adj-gueltig: At the airport the officer checks whether your passport is still not expired.
The bus ticket can be used until midnight and is accepted by the driver. It is still ...
You show the clerk a coupon, but it ran out last month, so it is no longer accepted. What word did the clerk say before 'no longer'?
a1-n-juli: It is the hottest month of the year, schools are closed and you go swimming at the lake. It is the seventh month.
You have your birthday between June and August. Which month is it?
Which month comes after June and before August?
a1-n-million: The lottery prize is a one followed by six zeros in euros. Which number is that?
A big city has 1,000,000 inhabitants. How many is that?
Your uncle says that it would cost a thousand times a thousand euros to buy that villa.
a1-v-gefallen: You try on a red jacket in a shop and smile. You say that it is nice for you, you find it pleasant.
Your friend asks how the film was. You say that it was enjoyable for you, in the sense that it pleased you.
The tourists say that the city is very pleasant to them. Which verb means that something is pleasing to someone?
a1-adv-plus: In the maths lesson the teacher says: two ... three is five. Which word do you say for the addition sign?
The weather forecast says that tomorrow it will be above zero, at five degrees. Which word could you say before 'five' for a positive temperature?
The shop clerk adds the delivery fee to the price. Which small word shows the addition sign?
a1-n-ehefrau: At a wedding the bride puts on a ring and becomes the female spouse of her husband.
A man introduces the woman next to him, who he married two years ago.
On the form, in the family status section, you write the woman married to the applicant. Which word?
a1-n-schule: At 8 a.m. the children carry their bags to the building where they have lessons from teachers.
After the summer holidays the building is open again and pupils learn maths and reading there.
Your six-year-old daughter starts at a place where she will learn to read and write.
a1-v-feiern: You get a new job, so you open a bottle of sparkling wine with your friends to mark the great news.
It is your birthday and you invite friends to enjoy music, food and cake together.
On New Year's Eve everyone is dancing and having fun at midnight. Which verb describes this?
a1-n-sonntag: On this day most shops are closed and many people rest at home or go to church.
The day between Saturday and Monday is the day when the weekend ends.
Your friend asks which day closes the week, right before Monday starts.
a1-adj-maennlich: On a form there are two boxes, one for female and one for the other gender. You tick the box for a man.
A zoo guide says that the lion with the big mane is a masculine animal, not a lioness.
The doctor asks about the gender of the patient: it is a man, so he writes down the word for 'masculine'.
a1-n-abflug: On the board at the airport you see that the plane to Madrid leaves at 10:45. What is the information about?
Your plane takes off in two hours, so you must hurry through security.
Your friend asks what time your flight leaves the ground. Which noun means the time when the plane starts?
a1-n-entschuldigung: You forget your friend's birthday and send her a message saying you are sorry. This is a way of saying sorry.
The student comes late and tells the teacher a reason why he was not on time, for example that the bus broke down.
After you push a person in the shop, you say 'Sorry!' What noun means this expression of regret?
a1-v-finden: You look for your keys everywhere and finally see them under the sofa. You come across them.
A friend asks your opinion about the new film. You say that you think it is great.
You search the internet for a restaurant nearby and discover a good Italian one.
a1-n-brief: Your grandmother does not use email. She writes by hand on paper, puts it in an envelope with a stamp and posts it.
The postman puts a paper message in an envelope with your name in your mailbox.
You write to the town office to ask a question. You use a sheet of paper and a stamp. Which word means this kind of written message?
a1-pr-er: You talk about your brother, who is at the door: 'Where is Peter? ... is at the door.' Which small word means 'he'?
You point to the dog and say that this animal is hungry. Which word for the male animal can also mean 'it' for a masculine noun?
Your friend asks about the new teacher. You answer that the man is very nice. Which pronoun replaces 'the man'?
a1-n-grosseltern: Every summer you stay with your mother's parents and your father's parents in the countryside.
At Christmas the whole family sits at the table: parents, children and the older generation, the parents of your parents.
A child draws a picture of the grandmother and grandfather together. What is the word for both of them?
a1-adv-dann: You say first you will cook dinner, afterwards you will watch TV. Which word means 'afterwards'?
The teacher says: first read the text, next write the answers. Which small word connects the second step?
A friend asks: if you don't come, what will we do next, at that point? Which word means 'in that case' or 'at that time'?
a1-n-schrank: In your bedroom you hang your shirts and jackets in a tall piece of furniture with doors.
In the kitchen you keep plates and glasses in a piece of furniture on the wall with shelves behind doors.
The moving men carry a big wooden piece of furniture with doors and shelves up the stairs.
a1-v-machen: The teacher asks what you will be doing in the weekend. You say you will be making a cake and doing your homework.
You ask your sister what she is doing right now, because you see her working at the table.
A friend asks you to prepare a coffee for him. Which common verb means 'to do' or 'to make'?
a1-adj-schnell: The race car passes the others at 300 kilometres per hour. It moves at great speed.
You need to finish your homework within five minutes, so you work at a high pace.
A friend says the express train takes only two hours from Berlin to Munich. Which adjective describes the train?
a1-n-fleisch: At the butcher's you buy beef and pork, and a vegetarian friend says that she does not eat this.
The recipe says: put the pieces of chicken, lamb or beef into the pan.
A hungry man is choosing from the menu between a dish with fish and a dish with pork. Which food word covers beef, pork and lamb?
a1-n-sport: After work you go to the gym, run or play football. What kind of activity is this?
At school there are lessons where pupils play volleyball and run. Which school subject is that?
Your doctor says that regular physical activity such as swimming and cycling is good for your heart.
a1-v-kochen: For dinner you stand in the kitchen and prepare pasta and sauce on the stove.
You put the eggs in a pot of water on the stove and wait ten minutes until they are hard.
Your father loves to prepare meals for the whole family on Sundays. Which verb means this activity?
a1-n-westen: In the evening the sun goes down in one direction. At the compass this is the opposite of east.
Your friend lives in France, which is in the direction left of Germany on the map. Which compass direction is that?
On the compass there are four directions: north, south, east and ... Which one is missing, the one where the sun sets?
a1-n-leben: The doctor says to take care, because staying healthy is important for the whole span between birth and death.
Your grandfather tells stories about his time on Earth, from his childhood until now.
A poster says: enjoy every day of your existence. Which noun means what we live from birth to death?
a1-n-sommer: In July you wear shorts, go swimming and eat ice cream because the sun is hot.
The season with the longest days and the school holidays comes after spring.
A friend asks which season is the warmest. Which season is it, between spring and autumn?
a1-adj-letzter: In a race you cross the finish line after everyone else; you are behind all of the others. Which adjective describes your place?
The bus driver says that the final bus of the evening leaves at midnight. Which adjective do you use?
The teacher says this is the end of the book, the page that comes after all the others. Which adjective means 'final'?
